output.explanation: Expanded terminal-state because geometry/font metrics and decoded protocol inputs concealed deeper derivations. Its central tree now nests inputs beneath retained-state mutations; terminal-geometry expands sizing, font resolution and padding, while terminal-decoding expands streaming decode and protocol continuation. Their shared reporting dependency is connected explicitly. Left data-core and interaction-values unchanged, preserving their ASCII and all existing edges, with endpoints moved where concepts moved. Checked the pinned checkout without modifying it. Corrected font features being grouped with font-grid inputs: they configure renderer shaping, not SharedGridSet metrics/cache keys. Also clarified handler-owned DCS/APC state, configuration-driven terminal updates, and resize pixel/mode behavior.

Consumers (references, not additional sources of geometry):
|-- Termio.resize: backend gets grid + Size.terminal while holding terminal lock [ref T]
|-- Terminal.width_px/height_px: columns/rows * cell pixels (resize saturates u32 overflow)
|-- Surface.posToViewport -> Coordinate.convert: subtract padding, divide by cell size,
|   clamp to grid; pointer pixels [external] become selection/report coordinates
`-- Size reports use current geometry when the decoded request is handled [ref D]
Font grids also carry resolver/glyph resources used by frame shaping [ref F, data-core].
Config reload preserves manually adjusted font size; otherwise takes configured points.
Scale changes rebuild the font grid, update padding and force pixel-level resize.
Font-feature options configure the renderer shaper, not SharedGridSet's metrics/cache key.

[D] Decoded text, VT actions and protocol requests consumed by the state updater
`-- Compute: Stream.nextSlice/next and handler protocol parsers derive and dispatch values
    |-- Printable runs and control-sequence actions
    |   `-- Compute: resume partial UTF-8/VT state; decode runs until ESC;
    |       printRuns emits printable runs and executes intervening C0 controls
    |       |-- Current output bytes
    |       |   `-- Compute: Termio.processOutput takes terminal lock -> processOutputLocked
    |       |       `-- PTY/backend output chunk [external; endpoint in L, data-core]
    |       `-- Stream.parser and utf8decoder state from earlier chunks
    |           `-- Compute: nextSliceCapped / nextUtf8 / consumeUntilGround advance state;
    |               nextNonUtf8 and OSC dispatch interpret escape parameters/payloads
    |               `-- Earlier bytes, partial codepoint/control sequence, OSC parser state
    `-- Completed DCS/APC protocol commands
        `-- Compute: StreamHandler.dcsHook/dcsPut/dcsUnhook or apc.feed/feedSlice/end
            |-- Hook/put/end actions from the same stream [ref above]
            `-- Handler-owned DCS/APC accumulation from prior chunks/actions
                APC completion can produce Kitty graphics or glyph-protocol requests

Dispatch relationships (decoded values are shared inputs, not all terminal mutations):
|-- ASCII runs -> vtPrintAscii -> Terminal.printSliceAscii; other prints -> vtFallible
|-- Cursor/mode/erase/style/link operations -> Terminal methods using prior state [ref T]
|-- DCS/APC completion -> protocol handlers; may update T and/or queue replies [ref W]
|-- Query parameters -> status/attribute/color handlers and size-report messages [ref W]
|   `-- Requested values come from T, handler policy C and geometry G [references]
|       Size queries schedule Termio reports; title query schedules a Surface response
`-- Title/PWD/clipboard/notification payloads -> Surface messages/policy -> host requests [ref H]

The handler is session-long; replacing it without copying its state loses continuation.
The inspector uses next(byte) per byte; ordinary output uses nextSlice (debug may be scalar).
processOutputLocked also schedules render, throttles cursor-blink reset, and wakes the
Termio mailbox if dispatch queued messages. These are effects, not decoded text inputs.
Unsupported actions can be ignored; vt logs handler errors rather than making parsing atomic.
